catalog_quote: Bakatik the vocalic allophones are determined by stress, position within a syllable or a word, or phonemic environment. Word stress in Bakatik generally falls on the word-final syllable. Thus, it is not phonemic. The allophones of vowels /i/, /ə/ and /u/ are articulated by involving the advancement of tongue root (ATR) when they occur in stressed syllables. ... They are integrated into the language intonation system to establish the stress forms of an utterance. Typically, Bakatik rhythm is syllable-based and its word stress is predictable. It generally occurs syllable-finally. The examples are shown in (4.4) where indicates the word stress. [sə-ne-ří] to work together (4.4a) /sə-na-ri/ involuntarily (4.4b) /a-bak/ (4.4c) /na-ba/ (4.4d) /pən-ta-jun/ [e-bak] head [ne-ba] to leave behind [pən-ta-jún] swing In the sentence level the unmarked intonation of Bakatik statements is rising-falli…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress is on the last syllable of the word ('generally'), so stress is predictable and non-contrastive; stressed vs unstressed position conditions vowel allophony (ATR advancement of high vowels and schwa in stressed syllables).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the snippets seen.
new_statements.exceptions: The hedge 'generally' implies exceptions, but none are visible in the snippets; the book's 'Suprasegmentals' section (not seen) may qualify the rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('word stress'); citation forms presumably. Snippet spacing normalized (Google renders '/ ४ /' for /u/ and puts spaces around punctuation); the sentence boundaries are Google's.
new_statements.identity_note: The stress statement is from Sudarsono's 'Bakatik Dayak language', which he describes as having c. 60,000 speakers in West Kalimantan (i.e. Bakatik broadly). Glottolog files Sudarsono 2002 and Azharie 2001 under beka1241 (Riuk Bekati', ISO bei), but a 2009 Anthropologica snippet calls Sudarsono's thesis one 'on Bekati' (Lara')', and the catalogue descriptions of Azharie 2001 and Hanye 1988 say their Bakatik is that of the Dayak Lara people of Kabupaten Sambas; the Lara/Rara variety has its own glottocode rara1235 (Rara Bakati', ISO lra). Which dialect(s) the 2013 phonology covers is not visible in the snippets.
